national.title: Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
national.summary: Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., was the first Black-owned gas station on Route 66. At a time when Black families needed the Green Book to find places to stay, eat, use the bathroom, it provided fuel and respite.
national.body:
Edward Threatt stands outside the Threatt Filling Station in Luther, Okla., off Route 66. It was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous highway, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation. Nick Oxford for NPR hide caption

During the Jim Crow Era, Black families traveling Route 66, the historic highway that ran more than 2,000 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, needed to carry food and gas with them. Most restaurants, gas stations and motels wouldn't serve them.

But there was one place they were guaranteed to find respite: a small, family-owned business just east of Oklahoma City that offered fuel, food and a place to stop for the night. The Threatt Filling Station , according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation , was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous Mother Road.

The iconic road from Chicago to California is celebrating its 100th anniversary. Follow along with the history of the "Mother Road" and efforts to save and honor it today.

national.title: Bleeding, birth defects: Congo residents sue over alleged mining pollution
national.summary: A landmark lawsuit in Congo sees 27 residents accuse a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine of poisoning their community and the government of failing to protect them.
national.body:
KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.

She believes pollution from the neighboring mine is responsible for her family's suffering.

She has lost three children. Two died at birth. A third suffered repeated nosebleeds before dying. One of her two surviving children has stunted growth.

Now she and 26 other residents are taking the company to court in a rare attempt to hold alleged polluters accountable in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are also suing the government, accusing it of failing to enforce environmental regulations.

Like other plaintiffs, she asked NPR not to identify her, fearing retribution from the company or government. Although the claimants' names are public in court documents, they want to avoid further exposure. Their lawyers also fear the plaintiffs could face intimidation from other locals.

"Our children are the first victims," she said, as the sun set over a nearby mound of mine tailings. "What we're hoping for is to see justice done."

The plaintiffs, whose case began Nov. 3, describe similar problems: contaminated water, nosebleeds, skin rashes, miscarriages and birth defects, which they blame on mining pollution.

The mine, known as COMMUS, is owned by Chinese multinational Zijin and lies in Kolwezi, a city of more than 500,000 people in the heart of Congo's copper belt, a southern region with vast mineral reserves.

national.title: Doctors struggle to save babies after parents refuse vitamin K
national.summary: Doctors are fighting an uphill battle against disinformation about routine vitamin K shots given to newborns in the hospital. It helps prevent a rare but devastating bleeding disorder.
national.body:
At least one family refuses the vitamin K injection for their newborn each day, on average, at Corewell Health's Butterworth Hospital in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Kate Wells/KFF Health News hide caption

Every time Torrie LeBlanc failed to persuade a parent to give their baby a vitamin K injection, she thought about the blood-soaked diaper.

It belonged to a newborn delivered last year, in the bustling labor and delivery unit where LeBlanc worked as a physician at the Corewell Health hospital system in Grand Rapids, Mich.

This story was produced in partnership with KFF Health News .

In the early hours the day after the baby girl was born, she suddenly started bleeding "from everywhere," LeBlanc recalled. Her eyes, nose, and rectum all suddenly oozed blood.

The girl's parents cried out for help from their hospital room. Nurses and doctors on the overnight shift rushed her to the neonatal intensive care unit, where they pumped fresh frozen plasma and other blood products into her small body, trying to replace what she was rapidly losing.

Her parents had declined a vitamin K injection for their baby, which is given to most newborns within six hours of birth to prevent rare but life-threatening hemorrhaging. With their baby on the verge of bleeding to death roughly 36 hours after birth, the parents agreed to let doctors administer vitamin K.

It worked. The baby survived, largely because she received treatment almost instantly, according to LeBlanc and an attending physician who helped care for the baby. Had the baby been at home when she started bleeding, they believe she would have died.

national.title: Democrats probe whether Trump Jr.-aligned businesses benefit from government access
national.summary: Investigators say companies with ties to Donald Trump Jr's investment firm, 1789 Capital, have profited since his father's reelection.
national.body:
Congressional Democrats, led by likely House Judiciary Committee Chair Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, are expanding their investigation into the investment firm 1789 Capital, which brought on Donald Trump Jr. as a partner days after his father's reelection to the White House.

Since then, investigators say the firm has grown from "a middling venture capital firm" with $150 million in managed assets to "the darling of the venture capital world" with $3 billion in managed assets.

Investigators want to determine whether the growth was boosted by the president's son leveraging political influence or government information to secure federal contracts and regulatory changes for companies with connections to the investment firm.

Congress House Democrat warns 13 Trump allies to save their records for upcoming investigations Trump Jr. told Axios last week that the timing of his hiring at 1789 Capital was coincidental, noting that he had already been working with founder Omeed Malik for years. He also said he draws a clear line when marketing and raising money for the firm.

"I make it very clear [to foreign investors] that I have nothing to do with government," Trump Jr. said. "[The president is] my father, but he's also busy and I probably haven't spoken to him in three weeks."

He also suggested he doesn't use or need government connections to make smart investments. "Trying to do the things that we're alleged to be doing every day, I think that would last for about two seconds before it was out there very publicly," Trump Jr. said. He added that the firm relies on teams of analysts to make investments in industries where there are obvious public and national security demands but relatively few companies who are able to meet those needs.

NPR reached out to Donald Trump Jr. for comment and did not hear back.

Regarding Raskin's request for documents from 1789 Capital, Bill Burck, an attorney representing the firm, told NPR, "We responded to Congressman Raskin back in September pointing out in detail the many flaws in his understanding of how 1789 has operated and a number of basic factual errors. He never bothered to reply. Facts are facts and Congressman Raskin has them wrong here but persists in his tall tales against 1789. These are personal attacks untethered to actual evidence."

national.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
national.summary: Nvidia had come under pressure from President Trump to reappoint Huang, whose comeback helped add $1tn to the company's stock value.
national.body:
Jensen Huang has been reinstated as the boss of Nvidia less than two weeks after he was forced to resign following the revelations of extra marital affairs, one of which was with a suspected Chinese spy.

The AI chipmaker handed its co-founder his job back, despite rejecting his initial offer to return, after pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Trump said he "made the deal" with the tech giant's board to get Huang his job back, but both the president and Nvidia are facing backlash from lawmakers.

But his comeback added almost $1 trillion to Nvidia's market value as its share price jumped 31%, ending ended a streak of losses on the US stock market.

Nvidia's gains helped boost shares in other tech companies and financial markets in Asia while European markets were flat.

However, despite the surge, Nvidia's closing price was still down from its Friday morning price amid investor concerns about the wider AI industry and future development.

But it is a dramatic return for the man dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" to the company at the centre of the AI spending boom.

Attention will soon turn to Huang's appearance before Congress next week, where the Nvidia boss will be questioned over his relationship with Alice Huang, alleged to be a spy for China, due to national security concerns.

national.summary: Pope Francis suffered a profound spiritual crisis in 2021-2022 linked to temptations to exercise power omnipotently, his diary reveals, adding that he overcame it by entrusting himself entirely to God's mercy.
national.body: Vatican City — Pope Francis saw the "gates of hell" when he realized the depths of the clergy sexual abuse scandal and experienced mystical visions of the devil throughout his ministry, according to excerpts of his personal diary published by the Vatican on Tuesday."The Private Diary of Pope Francis" also reveals the Argentine pope suffered a profound spiritual crisis in 2021-2022, connected to his own temptations to exercise power omnipotently. He overcame the crisis by entrusting himself entirely to God's mercy. The book, being released globally in several languages, offers a deeply personal and almost voyeuristic view into the mind and heart of Francis, revealing his innermost fears, insecurities, dreams and temptations that he kept hidden from the world. It shows him as incredibly hard on himself, lamenting his own sense of worthlessness and shame, and his utter trust in God to lead him, even from the depths of despair. The book was curated by one of Francis' closest aides, Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, the Argentine theologian who heads the Vatican's doctrine office. Fernández is listed as the author, as his comments contextualize Francis' diary entries.Fernández expressed concern to Francis' successor, Leo XIV, that the book would be "left forgotten in some storage," and was permitted to publish passages, noting that "the spiritual concerns present in his (Francis') heart are very clear and can do us good." Written in a leather-bound calendar used as a notebook, it starts in 1992, when Jorge Mario Bergoglio was auxiliary bishop of Buenos Aires. It continues through his time as cardinal archbishop of the Argentine capital and finally pope. The last entry is Aug. 18, 2024. Watch: Moment troops raid home and capture Mexican drug lord Close Newly-released bodycam footage shows the moment troops entered a house and detained a Mexican drug lord who had managed to evade capture for years.

The video shows armed personnel entering via a garage and finding Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, also known as 'El Chapo Isidro', who was on the FBI's most wanted list.

national.title: DR Congo says aircraft missing as rebels claim to shoot down plane
national.summary: A South African fighter pilot and a Ugandan officer are reportedly among those aboard the downed plane.
national.body:
The Democratic Republic of Congo says it is searching for one of its aircraft, after rebels said they had shot down a warplane in the east.

The military said it had lost contact with a small Cessna 208 cargo plane on Sunday following "poor weather conditions". The fate of the plane and its crew remained uncertain, it added.

On the same day, the rebel Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) said it had shot down a warplane that was on a mission to bomb Minembwe in South Kivu province.

Four people were reportedly on board, including a Ugandan and a South African pilot, who is said to have been captured alive.

It is also unclear whether the aircraft reported missing by the DR Congo military is the same one rebels say they shot down.

A statement attributed to army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba posted on X said: "UPDF had nothing to do with the aircraft that was shot down in Minembwe. We have penalized that company."

The statement did not identify the company or explain what penalty had been imposed.

Gen Kainerugaba later posted that "no Ugandan is allowed to work for mercenary companies in [DR Congo]".

national.title: What Jensen Huang's return teaches China's Xi about Trump
national.summary: Huang being back at the helm of Nvidia is no guarantee of relief for Beijing.
national.body:
Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has riveted the world - including China, where it has become the top trending post on Weibo, the country's biggest social media platform.

Most users are pleased to see the return of the influential billionaire, who declared that he loved China, before videos appeared online of him eating noodles and drinking milk tea during a visit in May. Some wondered why - in the video of him returning to Nvidia's headquarters - he is not wearing one of his leather jackets.

But to many, Huang's return, which is being dubbed one of the greatest U-turns of all time, seems like a vindication for China.

Beijing has dismissed claims that one of the women who had an affair with Jensen Huang had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, its version of the CIA, as a spy. Chinese state media has also framed the spy saga as a smear campaign orchestrated by China hawks in Washington. The Global Times, a Communist Party mouthpiece, described it as a "witch hunt".

Now the White House, and President Donald Trump himself, have said Huang poses no national security threat, although investigations into the spy allegations are still ongoing.

Xi will have learned many lessons from this scandal, especially about Trump's pressure points.

For one, the fact that Huang's reappointment came so soon after Xi's meetings last week with Trump in Shenzhen could be read as a sign that direct engagement is an effective way to influence Washington.

Trump has said the two men discussed Huang, but did not elaborate further. Beijing has not commented.

national.title: Chinese official sentenced to death for spying
national.summary: According to state-affiliated media, the official received monthly payments in exchange for intelligence.
national.body: A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country and leaking "top secret" information in return for payment, state-affiliated media reported.The convicted man, identified only by the surname Ma, had been recruited by foreign intelligence while working abroad, according to a report on Monday in an online account run by Gold Wall Press, a publishing company linked to China's National Administration of State Secrets Protection.The recruiter, identified only as "Kailin," met Ma frequently, originally on the pretext of learning Chinese."Kailin gradually shifted the focus of their discussions to politically sensitive topics," probing for China's operational and personnel details in another country, the report said, without specifying which countries were involved."Ma disclosed a large amount of sensitive information concerning China's institutions" in the unidentified country, it said.Kailin later introduced Ma to a colleague, who threatened to report that he had leaked information to Chinese authorities if he refused to cooperate.Ma agreed to work for the foreign intelligence network and signed a cooperation agreement that included clauses on "confidentiality" and "loyalty."He received monthly payments in exchange, and "a laptop for the purposes of sending and receiving intelligence," the report said.Ma returned to China after he finished his overseas posting and "embarked on a long-term career of espionage.""He would extract relevant content from classified documents and materials he came into contact with at work; in the evenings, after returning home, he would organize the information and send it via espionage websites," the report said.Ma stole and leaked "over a hundred pieces of intelligence" during that period, it said, without specifying how, when or for how long that lasted.He was "eventually apprehended" and a court found that he had received more than 1 million yuan ($150,000) in exchange for 35 pieces of information, some of which were "top secret," the report said.The report did not specify when or where Ma was sentenced or whether he had already been executed."This shocking case serves as yet another wake-up call," the report said."The tactics employed by espionage and intelligence agencies are becoming increasingly cunning" and included emotional manipulation and blackmail, it said.

national.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
national.summary: Hasina has spoken several times of her desire to return, but this is the first time she has set a date.
national.body:
Bangladesh's former prime minister Sheikh Hasina has said she plans to return home on 16 December, more than two years after a popular uprising forced her from power.

Hasina, who has lived in exile in Delhi since August 2024, has asked the Bangladeshi government to fly her back to Dhaka, her spokesperson said.

The announcement comes amid renewed unrest in Bangladesh, where supporters of her Awami League party have staged protests despite a ban on its activities.

But it's unclear how Hasina will return. Last year, a Bangladeshi court sentenced her to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on student-led protests that ended her 15-year rule . She denies the charges.

Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir dismissed the prospect of Hasina returning on her own terms.

"Sheikh Hasina will not be able to return to the country as an ordinary commercial passenger; she will be brought back in handcuffs," he told a press briefing on Tuesday.

Kabir also accused Hasina and Delhi of fomenting recent unrest in Bangladesh, alleging that they were backing "terrorist activities" in the country.

India's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment. In April, ​the ministry said it was ⁠examining Bangladesh's request to extradite her and that it wanted to "engage constructively with the new government and further strengthen bilateral ties".

national.title: India's 'cockroach' party leader says he was stopped from flying to UK
national.summary: Saurav Das said that immigration authorities at Delhi airport told him that his passport had been "flagged".
national.body:
A leader of India's "cockroach" party has said that immigration officials at Delhi airport stopped him from flying to the UK, where he was set to attend a series of events.

Saurav Das said he was supposed to board a flight on Tuesday at 01:00 local time (19:30 GMT on Monday) but was told by immigration officers that his passport had been "flagged".

It is not clear yet why Das's passport was flagged. The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

Das, who rose to prominence in India earlier this year after Gen Z-led protests , said that he had been invited by the Oxford Union to speak about the movement.

He said that he was also scheduled to speak at other universities in Cambridge and Edinburgh.

"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual [government] was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions," he wrote on X.

A federal home ministry spokesperson directed the BBC to airport authorities and the Delhi police for comment on Das's allegations.

Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), said in a post on X that she and Das had been invited by the Oxford Union but that her visa had been rejected a few days ago.

national.title: US Army to detonate toxic explosives in Iowa after Trump paused plan
national.summary: The US military plans to detonate five tonnes of expired explosives on Wednesday, after appeals court decision.
national.body:
The US military has said it will move forward with plans to detonate five tonnes of toxic explosives in Iowa after an appeals court cleared the way.

The plans to detonate the lead azide, a highly volatile compound that is reportedly at risk of exploding on its own, were put on pause earlier in the day after US President Donald Trump ordered the Army to not move ahead unless a court and the state's incoming governor agreed.

The plans have faced legal challenges and public outcry over potential health and environmental hazards.

Army Secretary Adam Telle made the announcement late Monday that the military would detonate the explosives on Wednesday morning, calling it a "consensus decision".

"Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa's current and incoming Governors say the call belongs to the experts," Telle said. "We are proceeding with the controlled removal in full coordination with all state, local and federal authorities, because the safety of Iowa's citizens comes first."

His announcement came shortly after the 8th Circuit US Court of Appeals ruled that the plans could move forward, finding there were an emergency reason and adequate safeguards in place.

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), which granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the material, has argued it did so because the explosion risk "presented an imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment".

Earlier in the day, Trump said he felt the "proper course is to get rid of this longterm problem but, at the same time, have ordered the Military not to do so until" both the courts and the state's incoming governor Rob Sand agreed.

President Trump has said the government won't move forward unless Iowa's incoming Democratic governor signs off, although technically the governor-elect's input is not required and he is not yet in office.Following the ruling, the Army noted Monday night that current Iowa Gov. national.title: A timeline of the Karen Read case
national.summary: Here's a look at how events have unfolded in the Karen Read case.
national.body: Karen Read was found not guilty of the most serious charges in her high-profile Massachusetts murder retrial in June 2025. In their fourth day of deliberations, jurors acquitted Read of second-degree murder and manslaughter in the death of her boyfriend, Boston police officer John O'Keefe. She was convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol.Read's first trial, which started in April 2024 at Norfolk Superior Court in Dedham, ended months later in a mistrial due to a "starkly divided" hung jury. After months of additional pretrial hearings following the mistrial, jury selection in Read's second trial began on April 1, 2025. The jury got the case and began deliberations on June 13, 2025.Read was accused of hitting O'Keefe with her SUV in 2022 and leaving him to die. Defense attorneys argued she was the victim of an elaborate cover-up and was being framed by a group of people that included law enforcement.Here is a look at the timeline of events in the Karen Read investigation and trials.January 29, 2022 – the night John O'Keefe diedShortly after midnight: Karen Read, John O'Keefe and a group of friends went to the Waterfall Bar and Grill in Canton on the night of January 28, 2022. According to prosecutors, Read consumed several alcoholic beverages. Read drove O'Keefe to the home of Boston police officer Brian Albert. national.body:
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.

Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.

Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".

The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".

Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.

"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.

Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.

King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.

Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.

The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.

Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry".

Meldrum in 2014 became the first person who was not a recording artist to be inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (Aria) Hall of Fame.

Tuku Nkosiyaphantsi found out his daughter had been killed from a post on Facebook.

It was August and he hadn't been able to reach 27-year-old Okuhle for days, although it wasn't unusual for her to drop out of contact from time to time.

Then one Saturday, two of Tuku's neighbours called him to say that they had seen that Okuhle had been reported missing by police on Facebook. They had also seen a photo of what appeared to be Okuhle injured.

"When I looked at this photo, I saw that the person in it was dead, and when I looked closer I realised it was Okuhle," says Tuku, 50.

After seeing the image, Tuku phoned a police officer he knew. The policeman confirmed the woman in the picture had been killed and her body dumped near a river in Kokstad, an agricultural hub in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province, in the east of the country.

But because the morgue was closed for the weekend, it wasn't until Monday morning that Tuku was able to identify Okuhle's body.

When he did, Tuku saw she had been mutilated and her face badly beaten.

Okuhle had two children, aged nine and three, and was a civil engineering student.

Thanksgiving is nearly upon us, when we will once again get to sharpen knives with our clueless relatives about national politics at the dinner table.

Hopefully, this year we may find some of our dear ones finally seeing the light, now that Donald Trump is a lame duck President, repudiated by Democrats and even members of his own party in the recent midterm elections.

"Why didn’t you hit me over the head with a frozen drumstick?"

Now, the final straw that many of them will be grasping is the notion that Donald Trump was sent to America by God, just as King Cyrus was sent to release the Jews from the Babylonian captivity in 538 BC.

Cyrus was a personal hero to many people, from Alexander the Great to David Ben-Gurion. Thomas Jefferson’s copy of "Cyropaedia," written about Cyrus’s career, shows substantial marginal markings that signify the degree of its influence on his drafting the Declaration of Independence.

Like Donald Trump, King Cyrus was a flawed man. At the age of 10, during a childhood game, he had the son of a nobleman beaten when he refused to obey his commands. Years later, after one of his horses drowned in the Gindarus River, a furious Cyrus set his army to spend the summer dividing the river into 360 channels.

According to the Greek historian Herodotus, Cyrus’s later years were marked by arrogance, which led to rash decisions. Did he by any chance impulsively deface the portraits of his predecessors in the palace gallery with crude, derogatory plaques? Trump did.

On the contrary, King Cyrus generally treated defeated rulers with remarkable clemency, often allowing local officials to retain power, in order to foster loyalty. With Thanksgiving only two days away, there is no question the north county region again came through to help neighbors for the holidays.

Within the last week, our newspaper has reported on donations collected by Brooks-TLC Hospital that will support FeedMore WNY partner organizations serving local communities in Chautauqua County. “We are proud to be part of Rock Out Hunger and grateful for the opportunity to give back to the communities we serve,” said Ken Morris, president of Brooks-TLC Hospital. “The generosity and enthusiasm demonstrated by our employees are proof of the commitment they have not only to providing exceptional care, but also to supporting our neighbors beyond the walls of our hospital. Every donation makes a difference and we are proud to see our team come together for such an important cause.”

In addition to Brooks-TLC, other community groups have donated to Chautauqua County Rural Ministry. Those include: Lakeshore Street Rod Association; the SUNY Fredonia boys' baseball team and community members from Pomfret and Fredonia during a weekend food drive.

“People in this county are very generous,” Street Rods President Dale Davis said.

Buffalo prepares to renew what has become one of the league’s marquee n
local.body:
AP Photo Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) runs onto the field during Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins in Orchard Park.

AP Photo Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III, center, runs with the ball during the second half.

ORCHARD PARK -- Having spent the past month beating up on backup quarterbacks and a variety of the NFL’s more inferior teams, Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills finally get a chance to begin validating their AFC-leading 9-1 record.

Buffalo prepares to renew what has become one of the league’s marquee non-divisional rivalries by hosting Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) in a Thursday night showdown to be played in front of a national TV prime-time Thanksgiving holiday audience.

Forgive Bills coach Joe Brady for not buying into the hype by suggesting Monday he approaches each game with the same level of importance rather than ride what he called “the roller-coaster of emotions.”

As theme-park fixtures go, the past 10 matchups since 2020 have featured plenty of breathtaking ups, downs and hair-raising loops in which Allen and Mahomes have combined to score 51 touchdowns (41 passing and 10 rushing).

And yet Brady did eventually deviate from his familiar refrain of referring to Buffalo’s next opponent as being nameless and faceless. Out of respect, he referenced coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo as being among the league’s elite.

Since 2020, Buffalo has the regular-season edge, going 5-1 with five straight wins. It’s in the playoffs where the Chiefs have owned Buffalo by going 4-0, including conference championship game victories in the 2020 and ’24 seasons.

local.summary: The city is currently without a contractor to dispose of the leaves residents collect, bag and set out on the curbside for crews to collect.
local.body: Buffalo does not have a way to dispose of leaves and the problem is piling up in a parking lot in North Buffalo. The city is currently without a contractor to dispose of the leaves residents collect, bag and set out on the curbside for crews to collect. Instead, the bags end up in a pile at the NFTA's LaSalle Station parking lot in North Buffalo. Buffalo's Deputy Mayor Benjamin Swanekamp tells me the pile is a holding station for the bags before being transported to a holding garage in South Buffalo. "Right now we have to either find a contractor willing to work with us, or as might be increasingly necessary, us to develop our own yard waste recycling program," Swanekamp said.The leaves were once dealt with by Geiter Done, a yard waste disposal company based in the Seneca Babcock neighborhood. But in 2024, the company was issued a notice of violation by the DEC after odor complaints. As a result, Swanekamp tells me the Buffalo Common Council did not approve a contract renewal with the company."When it came up for renewal, the Common Council rejected them two years in a row, so since then the city's been in the position of having to hold debris," Swanekamp said.So why doesn't the city just send all of this to a landfill? New York state regulations prohibit leaves and certain yard waste from being sent to landfills to prevent methane emissions. local.title: Holiday shopping rush brings increased concerns about package theft and scams
local.summary: Americans are expected to spend a record $275 billion shopping online this holiday season, creating plenty of opportunities for thieves and scammers.
local.body: With Black Friday just days away, the holiday shopping rush is about to kick into high gear. Americans are expected to spend a record $275 billion shopping online this holiday season, creating plenty of opportunities for thieves and scammers.A study by SafeWise estimates that more than 100 million packages were stolen nationwide in 2025. While that's down from the previous year, porch piracy remains a major concern.Meanwhile, the Federal Trade Commission says fake package delivery notifications are the most commonly reported type of text message scam.Amazon, the nation's largest online retailer, is preparing for the holiday rush by hiring more than 300,000 workers nationwide."This is our Super Bowl," Amazon spokesperson Owen Torres told 7 News.The company is offering advice to help customers protect their purchases.One recommendation is to take advantage of Amazon's package tracking tools, which allow customers to monitor deliveries and share tracking information with friends or family members who can retrieve packages if the customers aren't home.Customers can also provide specific delivery instructions, including asking drivers to leave packages in less visible locations."I kind of have the instructions to hide it behind one of my planters," Torres said. "It takes it away from street view and protects the packages out of sight."If a package is stolen, Amazon recommends reporting the theft to local police before contacting customer service through the Amazon app or website to explore possible remedies.Package theft isn't the only concern.Amazon says approximately 360,000 customers contact the company each year to ask whether an email, text message or phone call claiming to be from Amazon is legitimate.The company warns that scammers often create a sense of urgency, request personal information or demand payments through gift cards.Amazon recently introduced a new tool for its "Alexa for Shopping" AI assistant, which allows customers to ask whether a suspicious communication actually came from the company. Customers can access the feature through the Amazon app or Amazon.com.Amazon also recommends using its secure Locker delivery locations as an alternative to having packages left unattended on doorsteps.

local.body: As recent delays and a Delta outage rattle holiday plans, travelers at the Buffalo Niagara International Airport share their worries — but officials say operations are back to normal.Recent flight delays have travelers heading home for Thanksgiving weekend worried about their journeys.I caught up with Emma Lipshultz as she arrived from Miami, flying alone for the first time with her 3-month-old daughter. I feel for the airport employees. I feel for the airline employees, who really have to face the brunt of all of the anxiety and the disappointment," Banerjee said.NFTA spokesperson Kelly Khatib tells me operations at the Buffalo airport have been back to normal."Anytime that anyone's travel plans or wherever you're going is interrupted, it can be frustrating for people, but I think the biggest thing that people should remember is air travel is the safest way to go," Khatib stated. local.title: High Falls to light orange for domestic violence awareness
local.summary: The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.
local.body:
The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.

"There isn't always closure for a lot of women, and so by calling attention to this, we're hoping that people will just be more aware, and that women who perhaps are victims will feel more empowered to get out of the situation that they are in," says Bonnie Abrams, a past president and current advocacy co-chair at Zonta Club.

A 2025 report shows domestic violence incidents in the City of Rochester are 2.4 times higher than the statewide rates, and the Monroe County rates are nearly double the state numbers, according to the Willow Domestic Violence Center.

"Though domestic violence occurs on all social strata, you know, but I think that unfortunately there are more incidents because of people feeling powerless, and I think that that's perhaps one of the reasons that the statistics are higher here in Rochester, and that's another reason why we want to call attention to this issue," she explained.

Abrams says the word "Zonta" comes from the Lakota word meaning "honest" or "trustworthy". She says she wants everyone to know there are trusted people willing to help.

The Rochester branch is part of a national network that first started in Buffalo. They issue grants and other support to organizations that further its mission to improve the lives of women and girls.

The falls lighting will kick off the club's 16 Days of Activism that runs through Human Rights Day on December 10th.

The event starts at Genesee Brew House at 5 p.m. Participants will walk over for the falls lighting and a proclamation reading from Mayor Malik Evans' office. A local survivor of domestic violence will serve as speaker.

local.body: As fans around the country say goodbye to the late Fiona, who stole America's hearts in 2017 after she was born prematurely at the Cincinnati Zoo, the San Antonio Zoo paid special tribute to the beloved hippo with a goodbye letter from her long-distance "boyfriend" Timothy.It wasn't long after Fiona's first birthday that she received her first big dating request from Timothy the hippo in San Antonio. "I have seen your pictures and videos on the internet at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden and I think you are the most beautiful hippopotamus I have ever seen," a post from the San Antonio Zoo, dated March, 6, 2018, reads. "Perhaps we can meet someday and be boyfriend and girlfriend?"Just a few day's later, Timothy's post got a response from Fiona. "Fiona thinks you’re cute too, but it’s what’s on the inside that really counts!" the Cincinnati Zoo posted in response. From there, their relationship took off.While the hippos were never able to meet in person, they carried on a "long-distance relationship" for years, with Timothy sending Fiona gifts and making special posts on her birthday. It was far from a one-sided romance. Fiona even sent Timothy a "kiss" for his birthday in 2021. "Your kiss painting that you sent me was my fav!" the zoo posted after Timothy received Fiona's gift. "Thank you so much and remember I always think you are the most beautiful hippo I’ve ever seen!"Just like so many treasured love stories, Timothy and Fiona's has a tragic ending. Fiona died on Thursday after swallowing a hat that accidentally got into her enclosure. She was just 9 years old.After the news of Fiona's death spread, the San Antonio Zoo posted a special goodbye tribute to the beloved hippo from her biggest admirer, Timothy. I know your keepers and vets did everything they could to save you and for that I am grateful," the post read in part. "Besides being the most beautiful hippopotamus that I have ever seen, you inspired the world through your story of overcoming all the odds at birth, and millions of people around the world fell in love with you. local.title: Bills-Chiefs Thanksgiving showdown brings holiday twist to tailgating in Orchard Park
local.summary: Thanksgiving dinner and football are coming together in Buffalo this year as the Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in a holiday-night showdown.
local.body: Thanksgiving dinner and football are coming together in Buffalo this year as the Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in a holiday-night showdown.The Bills will host a Thanksgiving game for the first time in franchise history, adding another chapter to one of the NFL's biggest rivalries.And for some fans, the festivities will begin well before kickoff.Danny's South Family Restaurant on Abbott Road is preparing for a busy Thanksgiving, with owner Mark Ebeling expecting a full parking lot of tailgaters ahead of the 8:20 p.m. kickoff.The restaurant is adding a traditional turkey dinner to its game-day menu, with meals available for both dine-in and takeout."We got a lot of calls for turkey dinners, so we decided to add a nice turkey dinner," Ebeling said.Some fans are even planning to bring their own holiday traditions to the parking lot, with Ebeling saying several groups will be cooking turkeys as part of their tailgate celebrations.Ebeling has owned Danny's South for 29 years and said he's looking forward to the atmosphere."I think it's going to be the biggest game of the year. local.title: Leaders Made Here: How Western New York Maritime Charter School is shaping Buffalo's future
local.summary: Through a combination of academics, character development, physical fitness and leadership training, the school is preparing students to become confident, responsible leaders.
local.body: At Western New York Maritime Charter School, education goes far beyond the classroom. Through a combination of academics, character development, physical fitness and leadership training, the school is preparing students to become confident, responsible leaders.Serving students in grades 5 through 12, Maritime incorporates military-inspired structure through its Naval Junior Reserve Officers Training Corps (NJROTC) program. Cadets are encouraged to take responsibility, support their peers and develop skills that will serve them long after graduation.The school's guiding philosophy, "Leaders Made Here," is more than just a motto."I went from a cadet who was not on the best track at Maritime, and I had all the tools given to me to become someone better," said Cameron Barclay, the school's Cadet Commanding Officer.Maritime's approach emphasizes hands-on leadership, accountability and personal growth, giving students opportunities to challenge themselves while preparing for college, military service or careers in the workforce.The school's impact also extends into the community. According to their website, cadets completed more than 9,400 hours of community service during the 2025–2026 school year, while the Class of 2026 achieved a 94% graduation rate."What it comes down to is, can we make you a better citizen once you graduate from this school?" said Antony Washington, Master Sergeant in the United States Marine Corps. "We teach life skills, right? And that's exactly what most people need when they graduate from high school."Through education, mentorship and leadership opportunities, Western New York Maritime Charter School continues to demonstrate its mission is about more than preparing students for graduation. It's about preparing them for life.Learn more: Western New York Maritime Charter SchoolWATCH: Leaders Made Here: How Western New York Maritime Charter School is shaping Buffalo's future

local.title: This flu season is already way ahead of last year's pace
local.summary: With the holidays quickly approaching, health officials are urging people to get vaccinated.
local.body:
Flu season is already off to a fast and aggressive start both statewide and in Greater Rochester.

As of Nov. 14, Monroe County has reported 1,259 confirmed cases of influenza, more than six times the number of cases that were reported last year at this time.

There are also 129 flu-related hospitalizations and fewer than 10 flu-related deaths. State and county data trackers do not provide an exact number of deaths until the number exceeds 10.

In a virtual news conference Monday afternoon, Monroe County Commissioner of Public Health Dr. Marielena Vélez de Brown stressed the importance of vaccination.

"The vaccine may not prevent every infection, but it can certainly reduce your chances of getting very sick and lower your risk of ending up in the hospital," she said.

Monroe County's current flu vaccination rate is 26.5%, higher than the statewide rate of 22%.

The flu vaccine is recommended to everyone beginning at 6 months of age.

"With the holidays approaching, many of us will be traveling, gathering indoors, and spending time with family and friends," Vélez de Brown said. "So, getting vaccinated isn't just about protecting your own health; it's also about protecting the people you're gathering with."

local.title: Strong Museum's Dyson tapped as next Rochester Museum & Science Center leader
local.summary: Jon-Paul Dyson starts his new role Feb. 1.
local.body:
Jon-Paul Dyson has been appointed president and CEO of the Rochester Museum & Science Center by the institution's board. He starts Feb. 1.

Dyson comes to RMSC from the Strong National Museum of Play, where he was senior vice president for exhibits and interpretive resources. He was also director of the International Center for the History of Electronic Games.

In his new role, he'll be responsible for guiding RMSC's strategic vision, educational initiatives, and community engagement. The start of his tenure coincides with the launch of a comprehensive strategic planning effort.

entertainment.title: Billy Bob Thornton says he’s a holiday ‘purist’ as he brings back ‘traditional’ Thanksgiving at home
entertainment.summary: Billy Bob Thornton tried to have Thanksgiving dinner at a restaurant in the past, and he'll never do it again.
entertainment.body:
Billy Bob Thornton tried to have Thanksgiving dinner at a restaurant in the past, and he’ll never do it again.

During an interview with Fox News Digital about his new Fox Nation series, “The Mayflower,” Thornton opened up about his own Thanksgiving traditions and how his newest gig shows the actual events that unfolded in 1621, not what is taught in schools.

“Well, I’ve always been a little bit of a purist in terms of holidays and, especially when you have kids, you want to kind of, you know, keep that tradition going. So my early Thanksgivings were in Arkansas, and then after high school I moved to Texas and Houston,” he began. “I’ve always wanted traditional holidays and particularly Thanksgiving and Christmas. And we have that, my family and I always have a traditional Christmas and Thanksgiving.”

He continued, “But for Thanksgiving, a couple of times over the last decade, we went to a restaurant, and it just didn’t seem right.”

Thornton said his wife and sister-in-law were tired of the mess that Thanksgiving creates in the kitchen, so they proposed the idea that they go out for dinner instead.

“We get there, and it was just like, we do this all the time, what’s special about it, you know? And so this year, we’re going back to the traditional thing and there’s going to be a lot of cooking going on and a lot of football-watching,” Thornton said.

Thornton hosts and narrates “The Mayflower,” which is a three-part historical docudrama. It premieres Monday, Nov. 23, on FOX Nation.

Speaking to Fox News Digital, the Academy Award-winning actor explained that once he was brought on to this project, he learned about the reality of the journey on the Mayflower and the extent of the “pain, suffering and sickness” people endured.

Steve Martin and Martin Short had London in stitches on Monday evening as the star-studded premiere of Only Murders in the Building season 6 took over the Odeon Luxe Leicester Square cinema in central London. Selena Gomez wasn’t in town, but a lot of the British stars in the latest season of the Disney+ hit show, entitled Only Murders in London , walked the premiere carpet to the delight of fans who came out despite freezing temperatures.

The iconic comedy duo of Short and Martin was joined at the event by series regular Michael Cyril Creighton, along with Nicola Coughlan, Martin Freeman, David Tennant, Jim Broadbent, Olivia Colman , Simone Ashley, Geri Halliwell-Horner, Lesley Nicol, Anjana Vasan, Matthew Beard, Amar Chadha-Patel, Jane Horrocks, Sean Teale, Sharon Horgan, Jodie Whittaker, Jamie Demetriou, Richard E. Coughlan and Ashley actually brought fans the joy of a mini Bridgerton reunion on the cold London carpet.

Co-creator and executive producer John Hoffman also crossed the pond for the premiere celebration in London, alongside fellow executive producers Jess Rosenthal and Kristin Bernstein.

Before the screening of episodes 1 and 3 – because they feature more of the Brit faces adding much fun and color to the new season, Martin and Short warmed up the London premiere crowd in classic fashion. “I love traveling around with Martin Short because – no paparazzi,” quipped Martin. “What an honor it is for me to be standing next to someone who looks like a former women’s tennis [player].”

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By Billy Crystal: 'I Had Not Cried Like That Since I Was...'
entertainment.summary: Billy Crystal shares what it was like to lose his home of 46 years in the Palisades Fire.
entertainment.body:
On the television front, Crystal is known for hosting the Academy Awards and for guest appearances in shows like "Friends" and "Modern Family." A recent role of note is in Apple TV's "Before," where Crystal plays a child psychiatrist who is grieving a personal tragedy.

The actor is also a celebrated theatrical performer, having won the Tony Award for special theatrical event for his one-man show, "700 Sundays," in 2005. Crystal has won six Primetime Emmy Awards and seven American Comedy Awards. He was also honored with the Critics' Choice Lifetime Achievement Award in 2022 and the Kennedy Center Honors in 2023. Crystal is beloved for his versatility and quick-witted charm, which is why he is today's quote of the day.

Static Media "I stepped onto the grounds and fell to my knees, and I wailed. I had not cried like that since I was 15 years old, and I was told that my father had just died."

The above quote is from Billy Crystal's speech to the crowd at the LA FireAid Benefit Concert (via Fox News ), which raised donations for the Southern California wildfires in 2025. Having lost his home in the Palisades Fire, Crystal shared a hopeful message for rehabilitation while opening up about the devastating emotional impact of the disaster.

"Tonight, we're here together to thank them and all those who run towards danger while we run to shelter and safety," Crystal stated, offering his deep appreciation for first responders. After that, Crystal likened the loss of his home to the pain of losing his father as a young child. "I remember looking in the mirror back then with my whole life ahead of me thinking, 'What's my life gonna be like without him?'"

Losing a home you've painstakingly built over the decades is undoubtedly painful. It signifies the loss of a familiar life, one that can never be reclaimed after the tragedy. It is also a collective loss, with grief binding communities together.

While Crystal acknowledged the grim reality of the situation, he urged everyone to find joy whenever they can, as our pain doesn't define us. "Even in your worst pain, folks, it's okay, and it's important to laugh," Crystal said.

entertainment.title: Jimmy Kimmel Criticizes Trump’s ‘Fishy’ Support of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
entertainment.summary: "I'm sure it also didn't hurt that Huang donated $25 million to the big stupid ballroom he's building"
entertainment.body:
Jimmy Kimmel zeroed in on Jensen Huang on last night’s episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live , taking aim at Donald Trump ‘s unabashed support of the Nvidia CEO.

“Who doesn’t love a good comeback story?” Kimmel quipped of Huang, who was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia despite an ongoing investigation into multiple alleged affairs — including one with an accused Chinese spy and two with Nvidia subordinates. Trump took credit for the decision, telling CNBC that he personally called into an Nvidia board meeting and “convinced” it to give Huang, one of the president’s closest allies in tech, his job back.

“After 10 grueling days of forced unemployment, the board at Nvidia today voted to reinstate their former CEO, who, according to our president, did nothing wrong,” Kimmel recounted. “All this guy did was cheat on his wife with two employees and a Chinese spy. Who hasn’t done that?”

Kimmel explained that the board issued a statement saying they have “every confidence” in Huang. “Which, of course, had nothing to do with the pressure from our Silicon Man in Chief, who has at least 62 million reasons why he wanted his pal in charge. After the board made it clear that they were unequivocally moving on, Trump called them personally to harangue them. And if you think that sounds fishy, it’s not. It’s called being a good friend.”

He added, “There’s nothing unusual about a president who owns a huge amount of stock in a company putting his little carrot thumb on the scale in a way that immediately boosts that company’s stock price. I’m sure it also didn’t hurt that Huang donated $25 million to the big stupid ballroom he’s building.”

After sharing an AI image Trump posted of Huang holding up a red bra after an assassination attempt, Kimmel noted, “What a profoundly stupid time to be alive.”

entertainment.title: Veteran actor rips Hollywood as ‘boring’ and ‘tedious,’ says he prefers the South
entertainment.summary: "It was boring to us. It was tedious … it wasn't about anything."
entertainment.body:
Tom Berenger said he never liked the idea of living in Hollywood because he always felt that it was like a “company” town where everyone had the same job and talked shop constantly.

“I never lived in Hollywood,” the “Platoon” actor told Fox News Digital recently. “I started in New York in the theater, and I always lived there. And I knew all those New York actors, you know, John Heard, Chris Walken. And a few guys are gone: Brian Dennehy, Peter Weller. And we all hung out together at times, but none of us really liked Hollywood.”

They all saw Los Angeles as a “company town where all people did was talk about it all the time,” he explained. “I guess it’d be like being in Detroit if they all talked about cars constantly. I don’t know. But it was boring to us. It was tedious… it wasn’t about anything.”

He said New York is a “whole different place” that has an identity outside of theater.

These days, Berenger calls Florida home, which he said he vastly prefers to L.A.

“And South Carolina, it was better too,” he said of where he lived for three decades. “They have other jobs and real jobs, for one thing, and it’s not the same old chit-chat, I guess. They look different. The people are nicer… I could go on probably for hours if I had to.”

Berenger recently narrated “Ronin 3: The Battle for Sangin,” a docuseries about a platoon’s experience in Afghanistan.

The series was released on Veterans Day and is available on Prime Video.

entertainment.title: The Best Magnesium Supplements and What to Look For, According to an Expert
entertainment.summary: We asked a doctor to explain one of the trendiest supplements on the market: magnesium. Here's what she said
entertainment.body:
Magnesium is one of the most popular supplements on the market thanks to wide-ranging potential benefits like better sleep, stress reduction, and improved digestion. Much of this popularity has been driven by social media, including the viral #SleepyGirlMocktail trend. Plus, a slew of A-listers from Taylor Swift to Scarlett Johansson to Lenny Kravitz have also talked about taking magnesium to relax.

So what is magnesium? Like most supplements , it’s a mineral used by our body’s cells to function. It helps turn food into energy, strengthen bones, and support normal heart rhythm. Another key function of magnesium is sleep regulation, since the mineral helps calm muscles and the nervous system and regulate sleep-related hormones. That means taking magnesium may help consumers get better natural sleep instead of being sedated.

There are several types of magnesium supplements, and each binds magnesium to a different molecule, affecting absorption and how the supplement is used. “Magnesium citrate, chloride, lactate, and aspartate generally have better bioavailability than magnesium oxide because they are more soluble and more readily absorbed,” Dr. Martina Ambardjieva, MD, Ph.D., urologist, and medical expert at Invigor Medical , tells Rolling Stone . “Magnesium glycinate also tends to be well tolerated.”

Studies show that magnesium citrate may support digestion and bowel regularity, chloride muscle and nerve function, lactate energy production, aspartate muscle function and energy, and glycinate relaxation, sleep, and stress management. According to Ambardjieva, the recommended total daily magnesium intake is approximately 310 to 320 milligrams daily for women and 400 to 420 milligrams for men, including food sources.

In order to choose the right magnesium supplement for your health and lifestyle , Ambardjieva recommends checking the amount of elemental magnesium (the actual weight of the magnesium in the supplement) and avoiding unnecessarily high doses. The best magnesium supplements also have third-party testing, such as USP or NSF verification.

entertainment.title: Line Of Fire Reveals Major Family Secrets In Tell-All Thanksgiving Episode — EP Joshua Safran Teases The Fallout
entertainment.summary: The Hollingsworth family Thanksgiving serves up a lot more than turkey and sides. The show boss fills us in on what to expect when Season 1 resumes.
entertainment.body:
Courtesy of NBC Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Warning: This post contains spoilers for Monday's episode of "Line of Fire." Please proceed accordingly.

Even the most diligent of planners among us likely didn't start thinking about this year's Thanksgiving until a few months ago. But "Line of Fire" boss Joshua Safran and his team started planning the Hollingsworth family's explosive family feast long before that.

"We knew on Day 2 in the writers' room that everything was going to come out at Thanksgiving," he tells TVLine.

In the episode, which aired Monday, huge secrets that members of the family had been keeping from each other for ages are blurted out during the big meal. Mike and Jane's post-separation hookups! Micah's relationship with his Secret Service protectee! Russ's kiss with Brandon!

And then, at the very end of the hour, Jack appears out of nowhere to save Jane and Mia from getting shot!

"Our only fear was, would the audience wait that long for all the secrets to be revealed?" Safran tells me. He described a section of wall in the writers' room on which a bunch of index cards reminded the scribes what the audience knew versus what the characters knew. For instance, the audience has known about the romance between Secret Service agent Micah (Tommy O'Brien) and the president's daughter, Sydney (Savannah Lee Smith) since the NBC series' premiere; Micah's family learned about it as they passed the sweet potato casserole.

The show's writers would rip cards off the wall as the story progressed. "And then we got to Thanksgiving, and there were still, like, six of them," Safran recalls, laughing. "And then Tiffany [So], who was one of the writers who was always addressing that, went and just ripped them all off."

Episode 9, "Blind Eye," is the show's midseason finale. Thanks to a full-season pickup in October, the drama will continue with five more episodes in early 2027. Until then, scroll down to hear what Safran has to tell us about what's ahead — and which actor at the center of one of the show's hottest storylines wound up with a part for which he didn't even audition.

entertainment.title: 15 TV Shows Like Yellowjackets
entertainment.summary: Showtime struck gold with Yellowjackets. For longtime fans of the series, here are 15 other shows to check out immediately.
entertainment.body:
Showtime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover The "Yellowjackets" are back on Paramount+ and serving up a final season of thrills for fans who have been following this team since 2021. Whether this last supper leaves us satisfied or starving remains to be seen — either way, there's no question in our mind that we'll be hungry for more after the finale.

If you don't decide to immediately rewatch the show from the beginning (to see if all those fan theories really add up) , TVLine has a whole lineup of series tailored to your particular cravings. "Yellowjackets" combined the mystery-box and supernatural survival of "Lost" and the unforgiving social deconstruction of "Lord of the Flies" and injected the final product with themes of trauma, guilt, and girlhood. As hard as it might seem to find a show that feels that fresh, we've assembled a list of 15 options that work from this same playbook. From the show's structural ancestors to its peers in the streaming age, these series explore the cost of making it through wildernesses both literal and metaphorical.

CBS Admittedly, "Under the Dome" doesn't have anywhere close to the same critical reputation as "Yellowjackets." The CBS series, adapted from a Stephen King novel by "Lost" writer-producer Brian K. Vaughan, is ranked at the bottom of our list of King's best book-to-screen shows . The legendary author himself has even expressed apparent disappointment , though he was originally defensive of what Vaughan and co. had managed to do under the constraints of network TV.

All that being said, it deserves to be talked about alongside "Yellowjackets" due to their thematic ties. In "Under the Dome," a small town is inexplicably trapped by a mysterious, near-invisible domed barrier that separates it from the outside world. When salvation starts to feel distant, the citizens trapped inside begin questioning the structure of their society, challenging the status quo for reasons altruistic and selfish ("Breaking Bad" alum Dean Norris is perfectly cast as a used-car salesman who attempts to seize power amidst chaos). Both shows explore what leadership, justice, and community become when boundaries we take for granted are stripped away.

NBC "Manifest" is in some ways the direct opposite of "Yellowjackets." It's essentially a show about a plane avoiding desert-island tropes entirely (an all but outright riff on "Lost") and crashing straight into the fallout at home. After a bit of turbulence on an otherwise uneventful trip, passengers on a commercial flight land in New York only to discover that they've apparently been missing for over five years. The entire manifest was presumed dead — children on the plane stayed the same age, while those at home grew up; spouses moved on and found new partners; and the passengers start to realize they're all connected in strange, spiritual ways.

The 88-year-old and 56-year-old tied the knot in 2016 after meeting in 2005 when the Taxi alum—who was previously married four times—met her at the Santa Barbara Film Festival.

“I’ve been with him almost 22 years. My head’s full with a bunch of stupid stuff that you see on the internet,” she shared with People in an interview published Nov. 2. “I watch how contemplative and in control he can be, and I’ve always been more hyper and outgoing than him.”

And those differences are definitely what they’ve come to love even more over the years.

“I appreciate his focus and his calmness,” Lisa said. “Because I’m very outgoing and gregarious. And sometimes he won’t talk. So it’s a balance.”

entertainment.title: Tom Brady Admits to Parenting “Mistakes” Raising His 3 Teenage Kids
entertainment.summary: Tom Brady knows that all parents drop the ball sometimes. Since becoming dad to son Jack, 19, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan, as well as son Benjamin, 16, and daughter Vivian, 13, with...
entertainment.body:
Since becoming dad to son Jack , 19, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan , as well as son Benjamin , 16, and daughter Vivian , 13, with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen , the seven-time Super Bowl champ admitted there are some losses among his many wins as a parent.

“Well, I’ve made a lot of mistakes,” Brady said on the Nov. 22 episode of the High Performance podcast. “So, a lot like quarterback. I threw a lot of interceptions. And with every one I’ve tried to learn.”

And with that effort, the 49-year-old added, “I hope I’m a better parent today than I was when I first started having kids. And hopefully I’m a better parent 10 years from now.”

So, what is Brady’s game plan for becoming the best dad he can be?

“The important thing for me in my personal life is to go where my kids are at, too,” he explained. “Not to say, ‘Hey kids, pay attention to the things I'm doing or what's important to me.’ It’s been a really important lesson for me over the years to go to my kids and say, ‘What’s really important to you? What’s driving you? Or what are you scared of, or how can I pay attention to the things that you value?’”

Finding ways to connect with his kids is a skill Brady said he developed from leading football teams during his 23 seasons as an NFL quarterback.

“Part of that is just being really open and present and also trying to be really relatable to the younger [generation],” he continued, “which I was very fortunate to learn over the course of my playing career.”

And now, Brady emphasized that he is simply trying to be “really present” and “non-judgmental” with his kids while imparting the wisdom he’s scored through his “years of experience.”

The International Emmy Awards , the global version of the U.S. TV honors, were handed out in New York Monday night.

The top prize of best drama went to French foodie-themed period series Carême from Apple TV. The series beat out Steven Knight’s Hulu boxing drama A Thousand Blows ; Prime Video’s Argentine political drama Menem ; and underdog sports drama Real Kashmir Football Club from Indian pay-TV group Sony LIV.

Best drama was one of the few categories where Netflix was not represented. Related Stories Movies How Iran's Pegah Ahangarani Turned Her Family Archives Into a Regime-Challenging Oscar Hopeful Movies 'The Odyssey' Leads Critics Choice Awards Below-The-Line Shortlists

Netflix went into the 54th International Emmys the clear frontrunner with nine nominations, including all four best comedy noms — for the Rowan Atkinson slapstick series Man vs. Baby ; the Spanish sitcom Old Dog, New Tricks ; Argentine satire División Palermo ; and Vir Das: Fool Volume , the latest comedy special from the Indian stand-up star . División Palermo won the award.

Still that prize was the only one that went to a program from the streamer.

Best actor went to Bobby Schofield for BBC drama Unforgivable , beating out nominees Javier Cámara, up for his lead performance Spanish dark comedy Jakarta for Moviestar Plus+; Ricardo Darín for Netflix’s Argentine sci-fi survival thriller The Eternaut ; and Ian Roberts for Prime Video’s South African road movie A Kind of Madness .

Best actress, despite Netflix boasting two of this year’s nominees, went to Belgian actress Mona Mina Leon, nominated for Flemish dramedy Holy Sh!t . Leon beat out Bárbara Mori from Lucca’s World , Park Ji-Hyun from You and Everything Else and Sheridan Smith for the Brit true-crime drama I Fought the Law from ITV.

In total, there were 64 nominees across 16 categories spanning 22 countries. Shrinking star Michael Urie hosted this year’s ceremony at the New York Hilton in Manhattan.

Read on for a breakdown of Monday's "Voice" results, including our thoughts about each performance, as well as official videos when available. Plus, find out which two singers won't be returning for next Monday's live Top 8 showdown:

We were surprised enough when "The Voice" announced that the Top 10 would be performing in duets this week, but were floored when we heard that BigCountry and Dakota Cohen would be taking on "Jolene," Dolly Parton's timeless ode to man-stealers everywhere. Both artists brought the grit and gravel for which they've both become beloved, though BigCountry's approach was flavored with considerably more country sauce. This was an incredibly fair fight, with both artists growling their way through the song, gradually growing to an explosive finish. Maybe this is nitpicky, but Cohen seemed to connect to the song a little more, making it feel like she was singing it to someone, whereas BigCountry's boisterous take felt more like he was singing it at us.

TVLine's grade, BigCountry: A TVLine's grade, Dakota Cohen: A

This week's unexpected team-ups continued with Ferryn & Brinkley joining Kyle Davis on the classic Dolly Parton/Kenny Rogers duet "Islands in the Stream." Then again, considering Davis frequently sings with his own daughters — who are similar in age to Ferryn & Brinkley — he felt surprisingly comfortable working with the young duo. And you knew the sisters wouldn't have any trouble with this one, given that they literally worked at Dollywood. In the end, the trio worked together quite nicely, with Ferryn & Brinkley matching Davis' more mature sound without sacrificing any of the tight, gorgeous harmonies we've come to expect from them. (Their little breakdown in this song was especially heavenly.) The whole thing felt like a fun throwback, with everyone on stage just sort of vibing out. But if we must declare our own personal winner, it did feel like Davis was the odd man out at times.

entertainment.summary: Derek Hough healed through dance. As the Dancing With the Stars judge looked back on the beginning of his path to becoming a professional dancer, he shared one of the darker chapters of his...
entertainment.body:
As the Dancing With the Stars judge looked back on the beginning of his path to becoming a professional dancer, he shared one of the darker chapters of his childhood with sister Julianne Hough while being raised in the suburbs of Salt Lake City, Utah.

"The neighborhood that we grew up in, we definitely just had some neighbors that weren't great. They pretty much terrorized my family in a lot of ways," Derek shared in his Nov. 23 documentary Symphony of Dance per USA Today , stating, "One of my neighbors was, for lack of a better word, just really inappropriate with me physically."

In addition, the 41-year-old explained of the traumatic period, "They hung me up in a tree by my ankles, put a gun to my head, spat on me, hogtied me up in a field and left me there."

As such, enduring the abuse led to "a lot of emotion" for the then-12-year-old, who was raised alongside his DWTS costar as well as their older siblings Sharee , 49, Marabeth , 45 and Katherine , 44, by parents Bruce Hough and Mariann Heaton in the Mormon community. Julianne has previously shared that a painful part of her upbringing came at the hands of a neighbor in their cul-de-sac who she said sexually abused her at age 4.

"I just didn't understand where I was going," Derek said in the Hulu project about his reaction to the harmful treatment. "I was kind of left to my own devices."

And at first, the trauma pushed the choreographer further away from his future as a ballroom pro.

As he detailed, "I was a 12-year-old. I would skip school. I would skip dance. I wouldn't go. My dad was at work, and my mom was off, and [I was] just floating around with no direction."

Fortunately, Derek was "relieved" when he met mentors Corky Ballas and Shirley Ballas —parents of DWTS coach Mark Ballas —who soon moved Derek, and eventually Julianne, to London to attend drama academy Italia Conti Academy of Theatre Arts.

entertainment.title: Antoine Fuqua Accused of Pointing Handgun, Using Antisemitic Slur in Assault Lawsuit
entertainment.summary: A spokesperson for the director denied the allegations and said, "It's not true."
entertainment.body:
Director Antoine Fuqua has been sued for assault and battery by a bar manager, who alleges the director struck him with a handgun and used an antisemitic slur.

In a lawsuit filed on Friday in California state court, the bar manager, William Rosenthal, details an altercation in February in which Fuqua and his group were denied entry to a Los Angeles bar because they were overly intoxicated. He claims the director “directed a racial and antisemitic slur” at him before the filmmaker and his son “pointed their handguns” in his direction. Rosenthal brings claims for assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress. He seeks at least $50,000.

In a statement, a spokesperson for the director denied the allegations. “It’s not true,” the representative said.

The lawsuit says Fuqua and four others, including his daughter and son, visited Good Times at Davey Wayne’s in Los Angeles on Feb. 14. After the group was refused entry by Rosenthal, he was spat on by a member of the group and threatened by Fuqua’s daughter, according to the complaint. They left the establishment, the lawsuit says.

Roughly an hour later, Fuqua returned and confronted Rosenthal about pepper spraying his daughter. Rosenthal denied the accusation and was hit in the face with a handgun by the director, who later used an antisemitic slur and threatened to kill the bar manager. From there, the altercation escalated, with Fuqua’s son also pulling out a handgun and striking Rosenthal, the lawsuit says.

Rosenthal says he sustained a head injury, nose fracture and lacerations from the alleged assault and now has post-traumatic stress disorder and severe emotional stress. His lawyers say the injuries will result in “some permanent disability.”

sports.title: Jayden Daniels passed for 146 yards in fourth quarter after totaling 143 in first three
sports.summary: When the fourth quarter started on Monday night, the Commanders trailed the Bengals 17-13.
sports.body:
Daniels passed for more yardage in the fourth quarter than he had in the first three quarters combined on Monday night, delivering in the clutch in a season when he has frequently been criticized for failing to do so.

In the first three quarters, Daniels was 13-for-19 for 143 yards. In the fourth quarter, Daniels was 10-for-16 for 146 yards.

Daniels got better as the game went on. The Commanders punted on their first four offensive possessions, then scored on their last six. Their three fourth-quarter drives went 13 plays for 78 yards, 11 plays for 66 yards, and finally a sensational 64-yard drive that consisted of a 22-yard pass from Daniels to Antonio Williams, a spike, a 42-yard pass from Daniels to Williams, another spike, and the game-wining field goal as time expired.

sports.title: Dan Quinn: Scars from our late-game losses run deep, glad Jayden Daniels won it for us
sports.summary: "I couldn't have been more proud of Jayden at the end of the game," Quinn said after the Commanders' 22-20 win.
sports.body:
“Those scars run deep,” Quinn said. “There’s no question, failures in some. And I think those scars help.”

Quinn said he trusted Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels to have the ball in his hands at the end, and wanted to manage the clock in such a way that Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow would not be the quarterback with the chance to win it at the end.

“I didn’t want [Daniels] to not touch the ball at the end of the game,” Quinn said. “This is not a quarterback on the other side that you want to have holding it at the end of the game.”

Daniels has been harshly criticized this season for mismanaging late-game situations, but Daniels made two tremendous throws on the final drive to get the Commanders into range for their game-winning field goal.

“I couldn’t have been more proud of Jayden at the end of the game,” Quinn said. “To see those guys come through at the end, I thought that was one of our best team wins. I didn’t think anything could top last week’s but tonight did.”

The Commanders are now 4-5-1 and still alive in the NFC East race. And they have some confidence that if they need their quarterback to deliver in the clutch, he’ll deliver.

The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario. Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.) With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen’s entire career. Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top. In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North’s Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC.
